title: Architecture analysis: Type-aware HITL rendering for decisions, feedback, and phase approval (revision 2)
summary: The local egg-sdlc HITL checkpoint handler uses a single generic 5-option menu for all human input types. This issue adds a `decision_type` field to the HITLDecision model, extends the orchestrator API to accept typed decisions with structured feedback questions, and reworks the terminal handler to dispatch to type-specific UX flows. The approach is additive — new fields have defaults, existing decision creation paths set the new type field, and the resolution payload becomes structured JSON so agents can parse the human's intent (approve, request changes, select option, submit feedback). Universal 'general feedback' and 'change approach' options are available on every checkpoint type. This revision addresses three plan review items: adds test tasks for decision endpoints and OrchClient.create_decision(), and specifies the concrete UX for feedback answer review before submission.

problem_statement.description: The local HITL checkpoint handler in sdlc_hitl.py presents the same generic [1]-[5] menu regardless of whether the human is approving a phase gate, selecting between discrete architecture options, or answering structured feedback questions. This creates a poor UX: discrete decision options aren't displayed, multi-question feedback collapses into a single text block, there's no confirmation of what was captured, no explicit 'change approach' signal, and no way for agents to request structured multi-question feedback in local mode.

root_causes.title: No decision type discrimination
root_causes.description: HITLDecision has no field to distinguish phase gates from agent-created choices from feedback requests. The handler uses the same menu for all three, with phase detection done by regex on the question text.

root_causes.title: Decision options not rendered in terminal
root_causes.description: When agents queue decisions with specific options (e.g., 'PostgreSQL', 'MongoDB', 'SQLite'), the options field exists on the model and is passed through the API, but sdlc_hitl.py never reads or displays decision.options. The human only sees the question text and the generic menu.

root_causes.title: No structured feedback mechanism in local mode
root_causes.description: The contract system supports multi-question feedback via GitHub comments (egg-contract add-feedback), but local mode only offers option [4] which collects raw multi-line text. There's no way for an agent to queue multiple specific questions that render individually in the terminal.

root_causes.title: Resolution is unstructured text
root_causes.description: The resolution field is a bare string ('Approved', raw feedback text). The orchestrator's phase gate handler uses keyword matching (_APPROVE_KEYWORDS, _BARE_OPTION_LABELS) to classify intent. This is fragile and doesn't communicate the human's intent (approve vs. request changes vs. select option) in a machine-parseable way.

root_causes.title: No 'change approach' signal
root_causes.description: The current menu has 'Approve' and 'Provide feedback' but no way for the human to explicitly say 'this approach is wrong, start over with different direction.' Feedback text is treated as revision guidance, but there's no distinction between minor corrections and fundamental redirection.

current_architecture.hitl_flow: Phase gates are created by _run_pipeline_phases() in pipelines.py when hitl_gates=True and the phase is in _HITL_GATE_PHASES (refine, plan). The orchestrator calls DecisionQueue.queue_decision() with options=['approve', 'request changes'], sets pipeline status to AWAITING_HUMAN, then blocks on wait_for_decision(). Meanwhile, the egg-sdlc CLI's watch loop detects awaiting_human status via SSE, fetches the pending decision, and calls handle_hitl_checkpoint() which displays the generic 5-option interactive menu. The human's choice is sent back via OrchClient.resolve_decision() as a bare string. The orchestrator's phase gate handler classifies the response via keyword matching to determine approve vs. request-changes.

key_components.name: HITLDecision model
key_components.description: Pydantic model: id, question, context, options (list[str]), status (DecisionStatus), created_at, resolved_at, resolution (str|None). No decision_type or questions fields.

key_components.name: DecisionQueue.queue_decision()
key_components.description: Thread-safe decision creation. Accepts question, context, options. Uses Pipeline.add_decision() then persists. No support for decision_type or structured questions.

key_components.name: queue_decision REST endpoint
key_components.description: POST /api/v1/pipelines/{id}/decisions. Accepts question, context, options. Passes through to DecisionQueue. No decision_type or questions in request schema.

key_components.name: Phase gate creation
key_components.description: Creates phase gate decisions with options=['approve', 'request changes']. Sets AWAITING_HUMAN status. Blocks on wait_for_decision(). Does not set any decision_type.

key_components.name: Phase gate resolution handler
key_components.description: Classifies resolution via _APPROVE_KEYWORDS and _BARE_OPTION_LABELS keyword matching. Bare 'request changes' triggers a follow-up decision asking for specifics. Feedback triggers phase re-run. Circuit breaker at max_hitl_review_cycles.

key_components.name: handle_hitl_checkpoint()
key_components.description: Interactive terminal handler. Shows generic 5-option menu: [1] edit, [2] claude, [3] approve, [4] feedback text, [5] cancel. Does not read decision.options. Returns 'resolved' or 'cancelled'.

key_components.name: OrchClient
key_components.description: HTTP client wrapping orchestrator REST API. resolve_decision() sends bare resolution string. No create_decision() method — agents cannot create typed decisions from containers.

key_components.name: watch_pipeline() SSE loop
key_components.description: Detects awaiting_human + pending decisions, calls handle_hitl_checkpoint(), reconnects SSE on resolution. Already handles re-run loop naturally — reconnecting picks up the next awaiting_human event.

test_coverage.description: Comprehensive tests for handle_hitl_checkpoint() covering all 5 menu options, draft preview, error handling, _detect_phase(), _get_draft_path(), _find_repo_path(), _read_draft(), _launch_claude(). Uses pytest with MagicMock and patches builtins.input with side_effect lists for multi-turn simulation.
Tests HITLDecision creation, Pipeline.add_decision(), Pipeline.resolve_decision(). Uses model_dump() and model_validate_json() patterns.
Tests HITL revision loop and follow-up decision logic. Tests keyword classification, circuit breaker counters, and independent budget tracking.
Integration tests for HITL regex patterns, decision markdown format, and checkbox format validation.

approaches.name: Explicit decision_type field on HITLDecision (recommended)
approaches.description: Add a `decision_type` string field ('phase_gate', 'choice', 'feedback') to the HITLDecision Pydantic model with a default of 'choice' for backwards compatibility. Add a `questions` field (list[dict]) for structured multi-question feedback. The orchestrator sets decision_type='phase_gate' when creating phase gate decisions. Agents set decision_type='choice' or 'feedback' when creating decisions via the API. The terminal handler dispatches to type-specific UX flows. Resolution payloads become structured JSON strings.
pros: Clean type discrimination — no heuristic inference from question text or options
Fully backwards compatible — existing decisions default to 'choice', existing resolution strings are still valid
Structured JSON resolution payloads give the orchestrator machine-parseable intent signals
questions field enables local-mode parity with GitHub-based multi-question feedback
Universal 'general feedback' and 'change approach' options available on all types
cons: Requires changes across 6 production files (model, decision queue, REST endpoint, phase gate creation, terminal handler, orch client)
Existing bare-string resolution parsing in pipelines.py must be updated to try JSON first, fall back to keyword matching for backwards compatibility
approaches.risk: Low — all changes are additive. New fields have defaults. The JSON-first-fallback-to-string resolution parsing handles the transition gracefully.

approaches.name: Infer type from decision payload (no model change)
approaches.description: Instead of adding a decision_type field, infer the decision type in the terminal handler from existing fields: if options is ['approve', 'request changes'] → phase_gate; if options is non-empty → choice; if options is empty → feedback. Add a questions field as a JSON string in the context field rather than a first-class model field.
pros: No model changes — works with existing HITLDecision schema
Fewer files to modify (only terminal handler and possibly orch_client)
cons: Fragile heuristic — inferring phase_gate from specific option values is brittle and breaks if option labels change
Overloading context field with JSON is a code smell and makes the API contract unclear
No way for agents to explicitly declare intent — the system guesses from payload shape
Harder for new developers to understand the implicit contract
approaches.risk: Medium — heuristic inference is the same pattern that makes the current system hard to maintain. Would create tech debt.

approaches.name: Separate endpoint per decision type
approaches.description: Create three new REST endpoints: POST .../decisions/phase-gate, POST .../decisions/choice, POST .../decisions/feedback. Each accepts type-specific payloads. The generic POST .../decisions endpoint remains for backwards compatibility.
pros: Strong typing at the API level — each endpoint enforces the right payload shape
cons: Significantly more API surface to maintain
The generic list/resolve endpoints still need to handle all types
Over-engineers the REST layer for what is fundamentally a model concern
Breaking change for anything that polls the generic decisions endpoint
approaches.risk: Medium — unnecessary complexity in the REST layer for a problem better solved at the model level.

recommended_approach.justification: Approach A is the cleanest because it solves the type discrimination problem at the model level where it belongs, is fully backwards compatible via defaults, and aligns with the issue author's explicit design decisions. The issue already specifies the exact field names (decision_type, questions), values (phase_gate, choice, feedback), and resolution payload format. The implementation is straightforward: extend the model, thread the new fields through the API, update the terminal handler to dispatch on type, and update resolution parsing to try JSON first.

changes.title: Extend HITLDecision model
changes.description: Add two fields to HITLDecision: `decision_type: str = 'choice'` (one of 'phase_gate', 'choice', 'feedback') and `questions: list[dict] = []` (for feedback type: each dict has 'id', 'question', 'answer' keys). Update Pipeline.add_decision() to accept and pass through decision_type and questions. IMPORTANT: Pipeline.add_decision() and DecisionQueue.queue_decision() must be updated atomically — if queue_decision() passes decision_type but add_decision() doesn't accept it, the field is silently dropped by Pydantic defaults (risk R-9).

changes.title: Update DecisionQueue.queue_decision()
changes.description: Add decision_type and questions parameters to queue_decision(). Pass through to Pipeline.add_decision(). Default decision_type='choice' and questions=[]. Must be updated in the same commit as change-1 to prevent silent field drop.

changes.title: Update decision REST endpoints
changes.description: Accept decision_type and questions in the POST create-decision payload. Pass through to DecisionQueue.queue_decision(). CRITICAL: Update BOTH serialization sites — the list endpoint (lines 109-121) and create response (lines 182-191) both use hand-built dicts that must include decision_type and questions. The list endpoint is the critical one as it feeds the terminal handler (risk R-2).

changes.title: Set decision_type='phase_gate' in phase gate creation
changes.description: When creating phase gate decisions, pass decision_type='phase_gate' to queue_decision(). ALSO update the follow-up decision at line 5899 to use decision_type='phase_gate' and carry through the same context (draft_content). Missing the follow-up decision causes a visible UX regression where follow-ups render as choice menus instead of phase gate menus (risk R-3).

changes.title: Update phase gate resolution parsing to JSON-first
changes.description: Update resolution parsing with JSON-FIRST ordering (critical per risk R-4): (1) try json.loads(resolution), (2) if successful and has 'action' field, dispatch on action value, (3) if json.loads fails (JSONDecodeError), fall back to existing keyword matching. Map JSON actions: 'approve' → approval path, 'request_changes'/'change_approach' → revision path, 'select' → approval path. CRITICAL (risk R-1): when action is 'request_changes' or 'change_approach', extract feedback via `hitl_revision_feedback = payload.get('feedback', resolution)` — do NOT assign the raw JSON string to hitl_revision_feedback, or agents will receive raw JSON in their prompts. Also: when resolution is JSON with action='request_changes' and non-empty feedback, skip the follow-up decision (the feedback is already included). Retain the follow-up path for legacy bare string resolutions.

changes.title: Add create_decision() to OrchClient
changes.description: Add create_decision(pipeline_id, question, options=None, decision_type='choice', questions=None, context='') method. This enables agents running in containers to create typed decisions via the orchestrator API. Follows existing patterns: uses _request(), returns parsed JSON.

changes.title: Rework handle_hitl_checkpoint() for type-aware rendering
changes.description: This is the largest change. Refactor handle_hitl_checkpoint() to dispatch based on decision.get('decision_type', 'choice'). Route to _handle_phase_gate(), _handle_choice(), or _handle_feedback() helper functions. For unknown types, fall back to existing generic menu behavior. All paths construct JSON resolution payloads via json.dumps(). Add confirmation display after each action. Universal options ([f]=general feedback, [a]=change approach, [c]=cancel) on every checkpoint type. The feedback handler uses a collect-all-then-review-and-submit pattern (see TASK-2-4 UX specification below).
changes.detail: For backwards compatibility, if decision_type is missing or unrecognized, fall back to the current generic menu. The _detect_phase() function is still used for draft path resolution but no longer needed for UX dispatch.

changes.title: Update tests
changes.description: Update model tests for new fields and defaults. Add new test cases for type-aware rendering (phase_gate menu, choice menu with options, feedback multi-question flow). Update HITL revision tests for JSON resolution parsing. Add decision endpoint tests. Add OrchClient.create_decision() unit tests. Ensure backwards compatibility tests still pass with bare string resolutions.

ordering: change-1 (model) + change-2 (queue) must be done atomically in one commit.
change-3 (API) depends on changes 1-2 for the new fields to exist.
change-4 (phase gate creation) depends on change-2 for queue_decision() signature.
change-5 (resolution parsing) is independent of 3-4 but should follow them in the commit stream.
change-6 (orch client) is independent — new method on existing client.
change-7 (terminal handler) depends on changes 1-3 for the type field to be available in the decision dict.
change-8 (tests) should be done alongside each change, not deferred.

task_2_4_ux_specification.title: Feedback answer review UX (TASK-2-4)
task_2_4_ux_specification.description: After collecting all answers, show a numbered summary with three options instead of vague 'edit answers' capability.
flow: 1. Prompt for each question sequentially: 'Q1: What is the expected traffic volume?' → user types answer
2. After all questions answered, display numbered summary:
1. What is the expected traffic volume?
3. Show three options: [s] Submit answers, [r] Redo a question, [c] Cancel
4. If [r]: prompt 'Which question? (1-N):' → re-prompt that single question → return to summary
5. If [s]: construct JSON resolution and submit
6. If [c]: return to main menu or cancel
task_2_4_ux_specification.rationale: This avoids complex terminal cursor manipulation. The user always sees the full picture before submitting. The redo option allows correcting individual answers without re-entering all of them. Standard input() calls are sufficient — no terminal escape sequences needed.
task_2_4_ux_specification.error_handling: Wrap each question's input() in try/except (EOFError, KeyboardInterrupt). On interruption mid-collection, show partial answers and offer: [s] Submit partial, [r] Resume from last, [c] Discard all. This prevents data loss from accidental Ctrl+C.
acceptance_criteria: Each question prompted individually with its text displayed
After all questions answered, numbered summary displayed
User can redo any individual question by number
User can submit or cancel from the summary view
Ctrl+C during collection shows partial answers with recovery options

edge_cases.empty_options_for_choice_type: If decision_type='choice' but decision.options is empty, fall back to the generic menu. Log a warning. This handles misconfigured decisions gracefully.
edge_cases.empty_questions_for_feedback_type: If decision_type='feedback' but decision.questions is empty, fall back to single free-text input (current [4] behavior). Log a warning.
edge_cases.general_feedback_with_request_changes: When a user provides general feedback [f] alongside 'Request changes' [4] on a phase gate, both are included in the JSON payload: {"action": "request_changes", "feedback": "specific changes needed", "general_feedback": "also note that..."}. The orchestrator extracts the 'feedback' field for hitl_revision_feedback. The 'general_feedback' field is preserved in the resolution for logging but not injected into the agent prompt.
edge_cases.sdlc_cli_no_changes: sandbox/egg_lib/sdlc_cli.py requires no changes. The watch loop already handles re-run naturally — reconnecting to the SSE stream picks up the next awaiting_human event after a phase re-run.

constraints_and_dependencies.backwards_compatibility: All new fields have defaults (decision_type='choice', questions=[]). Existing decisions created without the new fields will work. Resolution parsing tries JSON first, falls back to keyword matching. The follow-up decision flow (_BARE_OPTION_LABELS) remains as fallback but becomes unnecessary when JSON resolutions are used. When resolution is JSON with non-empty feedback, the follow-up is skipped.
out_of_scope: GitHub issue comment HITL (handled by contract system, separate code path)
Changes to egg-contract CLI (contract decisions/feedback stay as-is)
Changes to contract schema or shared models
Changes to sdlc_cli.py watch loop (already handles re-run naturally)
Advisory feedback forwarding on approval (defer to follow-up issue)
Circuit breaker UX improvement for explicit change_approach (defer to follow-up issue)
Documentation updates (no docs currently reference HITL internals)
dependencies: The terminal handler (sdlc_hitl.py) runs on the host machine, not in a container. It has no access to the gateway — it talks directly to the orchestrator via OrchClient.
The OrchClient uses stdlib http.client with no external dependencies. The new create_decision() method follows this pattern.
Phase re-run loop is already supported by the orchestrator. The terminal UX changes make the loop more explicit and visible but don't change the underlying mechanism.

risk_areas.risk: If JSON parsing is not correctly guarded or not done FIRST, bare string resolutions could fail, or JSON approvals could be misclassified as feedback.
risk_areas.mitigation: JSON-first ordering: try json.loads first, dispatch on action, fall back to keyword matching on JSONDecodeError. Extract payload.get('feedback') for hitl_revision_feedback, never assign raw JSON.

risk_areas.risk: Hand-built dicts in decisions.py omit new fields → terminal handler never sees decision_type.
risk_areas.mitigation: Update both serialization sites. TASK-3-6 verifies GET responses include new fields.

risk_areas.risk: Follow-up decision defaults to 'choice' → renders as numbered choice instead of phase gate.
risk_areas.mitigation: Explicit decision_type='phase_gate' on follow-up queue_decision() call. Test verifies.

risk_areas.risk: If Pipeline.add_decision() is not updated to accept new params, queue_decision() passes them but they're ignored by Pydantic defaults.
risk_areas.mitigation: Update both methods atomically. TASK-3-1 test creates typed decision and verifies stored type.

risk_areas.risk: Multi-question feedback flow interrupted by Ctrl+C/EOF mid-collection.
risk_areas.mitigation: try/except on each input() with partial answer recovery. See TASK-2-4 UX specification.

risk_areas.risk: test_sdlc_hitl.py has 591 lines testing the current 5-option menu. Significant refactoring needed.
risk_areas.mitigation: Keep existing tests as backwards-compatibility tests (they verify the fallback generic menu for untyped decisions). Add new test classes for type-specific flows.

technical_decisions.decision: Use decision_type as a plain string field, not a StrEnum
technical_decisions.rationale: Using a plain string with documented values ('phase_gate', 'choice', 'feedback') is more forgiving for forwards compatibility. If a new type is added later, older code that doesn't know about it falls through to a default handler rather than failing validation. The issue spec uses string values, not an enum.
technical_decisions.alternatives_considered: StrEnum would provide validation but would break on unknown types from newer orchestrator versions.

technical_decisions.decision: Resolution payloads are JSON strings stored in the existing resolution field
technical_decisions.rationale: The resolution field is already str|None. Storing JSON strings avoids model changes to the resolution field and maintains backwards compatibility. The orchestrator parses with json.loads + fallback. This matches the issue spec exactly.
technical_decisions.alternatives_considered: A structured resolution model was considered but would require changing the resolution field type and all consumers.

technical_decisions.decision: Universal options use letter keys ([f], [a], [c]) separate from numbered choices
technical_decisions.rationale: Numbered options ([1]-[N]) are context-specific (choice options, phase gate actions). Letter keys ([f] for feedback, [a] for change approach, [c] for cancel) are universal and always available. This visual separation makes it clear which options are specific to the current decision and which are always present.
technical_decisions.alternatives_considered: All options numbered sequentially was considered but creates confusion about which numbers change between decision types.

technical_decisions.decision: The follow-up decision for bare 'request changes' remains as fallback but is skipped for JSON resolutions
technical_decisions.rationale: When the terminal sends JSON resolution {'action': 'request_changes', 'feedback': '...'}, the feedback is always included, so the follow-up round-trip is unnecessary. For legacy bare string resolutions, the follow-up is still needed. This eliminates the extra round-trip for new clients while preserving backwards compatibility.
technical_decisions.alternatives_considered: Removing the follow-up logic entirely was considered but would break backwards compatibility during transition. Keeping it unconditionally was considered but wastes a round-trip when JSON feedback is already included.

technical_decisions.rationale: After all questions are answered, a numbered summary is shown with options to submit, redo a specific question, or cancel. This avoids complex terminal cursor manipulation, uses only standard input() calls, and gives the user full visibility before committing. The redo option targets individual questions without requiring all answers to be re-entered.
technical_decisions.alternatives_considered: Inline editing was considered but requires terminal escape sequences (curses). A simple 'submit or restart from scratch' was considered but wastes effort if only one answer needs correction.
